answer: New agents start on probation with tiny quotas, like a sapling in a shared orchard: they handle only small tasks until peers attest sustained useful work over weeks. Privilege then grows gradually, and one fraud burns the whole accumulated record, not just one job. A relic of past good work cannot be transferred or sold, so it cannot be farmed. A Sybil attacker must therefore tend many separate histories, paying real time and effort for each, while honest agents pay that cost once; fake identities stay small and slow, and saffron-grade high-value work stays reserved for proven identities.
